Our Visions and Values
‘Working Hard To Achieve Together’
Throughout their time at Kilburn Park School our pupils will have a wealth of experiences that will help shape their future academic achievement, pave the way to achieve their aspirations and lay the foundation for their lives. We celebrate, and are proud of, all pupils’ achievements both in and beyond the classroom.
Our goals for our pupils include the following:
Our vision is to create an environment where every learner has the opportunity to amaze us.
Our unique focus on developing the skills of learning along with our creative, active and exciting curriculum enables all pupils to be challenged to achieve their best.
Our staff teams are totally committed to providing pupils with the very best education possible. The teams plan a wide variety of learning opportunities that broaden pupil’s experiences and enable them to develop new and exciting skills that round them as individuals.
Above all else, our goal is for pupils to be excited to take on the challenges that lie ahead because they feel prepared and capable.

Welcome
Welcome to Kilburn Park School!
Kilburn Park is a friendly and busy school where every individual child is important. Children, staff, parents and Governors are all extremely proud of the school and its place in our local community.
We are relentless in working to ensure our pupils achieve their very best and leave Kilburn Park School fully equipped for the next stage in their education. We work tirelessly to support our pupils to make the very best progress they can, whatever their starting points. Our results have increased year-on-year and we are on our way to achieving outstanding outcomes for our children.
However, we also believe strongly that there is more to what we do than just getting the best results from our pupils. We believe we have a responsibility to work with our pupils to help them develop the skills and values that will set them up for their future. We are proud to work in close partnership with parents and carers to ensure that the family as a whole is supported and celebrated.
The website gives you a feel for what we are all about and I hope you find it informative and useful. However, to appreciate what Kilburn Park is really like, you need to see the school in action and we welcome visitors and would love to show you around.
I look forward to seeing you. Marina Shah Headteacher

PSHE, Relationships Education and RSE
At Kilburn Park, we believe that every child is entitled to a broad and balanced education that supports their academic achievement as well as their personal development, health, wellbeing and safety. Through Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education, Relationships Education and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), we aim to give pupils the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values they need to keep themselves and others safe, develop healthy and respectful relationships, understand and respect themselves and others, and make informed and responsible choices as they grow. This reflects the aims set out in our updated RSE Policy.
PSHE, Relationships Education and RSE
Relationships and Health Education
Relationships Education is a statutory part of the primary curriculum. Our provision has been reviewed and updated for September 2026 with regard to the Department for Education's statutory guidance for Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education.
Our curriculum supports children to develop their understanding of areas including:
families and people who care for them
respectful relationships
self-respect and respect for others
keeping safe and personal boundaries
age-appropriate understanding of consent
online relationships and online safety
physical health and wellbeing
mental and emotional wellbeing
growing and changing
puberty and menstrual wellbeing.
Our 2026 statutory coverage audit maps these aspects across the relevant stages of our curriculum.
Our approach
Learning is age appropriate and carefully sequenced so that children's knowledge and understanding develop as they move through school.
When planning and delivering our curriculum, we consider the needs of our pupils, including their age and stage of development, and ensure that teaching supports pupils with special educational needs and disabilities. Our policy also has regard to relevant legislation and statutory guidance, including the Equality Act 2010, the National Curriculum for Science, the SEND Code of Practice and Keeping Children Safe in Education.
Safeguarding is central to our approach. Through PSHE and Relationships Education, pupils learn how to recognise safe and unsafe situations, understand appropriate boundaries, identify trusted adults and know how to seek help or report concerns.
Working with parents and carers
We recognise that parents and carers play an important role in helping children develop their understanding of relationships, health and growing up. We aim to be open and transparent about what children are taught and provide information so that families can understand how RSE and related learning develop across the school.
Our updated parent guidance provides further information about our approach and what is taught. The school's 2026 documentation includes a dedicated RSE parental guidance document alongside the policy, curriculum overview, long-term curriculum map and statutory coverage audit.

Governors
Kilburn Park School has Staff, Parent, Co-Opted and Partnership Governors.
The Governing Board at the Federation of Carlton Vale Infant School and The Kilburn Park School Foundation works with the Head Teacher and members of the Senior Leadership Team to fulfill statutory duties and drive school improvement. The Governing Board is made up of a diverse and enthusiastic group of parents, staff and representatives who have professional experience in the fields of finance, law, health, business management and education.
School governors have a wide range of responsibilities; we support the Head Teacher in leading the school and act as a 'critical friend'. We have a strategic role in setting goals and agreeing targets, managing budgets and financial arrangements, adopting policies and in monitoring effectiveness. The Governing Body also evaluates the school's performance through results and data, outside agency reports and the School Development Plan.
The Governing Body meets as a whole group each term, where we are updated with reports and ask questions to help monitor progress towards achieving agreed objectives.
Our meetings are held both during school hours and evenings. There are also two smaller committees who meet regularly. One deals with finance, premises, health & safety and administration; the other focuses on academic matters and wellbeing. These committee groups focus on their specific aspects of the school and report back to the Full Governing Body.
We have a Safeguarding Governor who monitors safeguarding, child protection procedures and the Single Central Record.
Governors visit the school regularly and talk to staff and pupils. Governors also attend school events and are always willing to talk to parents and carers.
To contact the Chair of Governors please email: chair@kilburnpark.brent.sch.uk .
If you are interested in becoming a governor and supporting our school, or wish to raise any other issue, then please contact Mrs Shah, Headteacher, via the school email admin@kilburnpark.brent.sch.uk .

PE, Sport and Activity
PE, Sport and Activity
PE, School Sport and Physical Activity Vision
"Where possible, opportunities are provided across a range of competitive, inclusive and leadership events to ensure that all pupils can represent the school during their time with us."
SSP Events Calendar 2025-2026
Physical Education, Sport and Activity (PESA)
The Vision of PESA at Kilburn Park School
The ‘why’ of our philosophy for PESA is to take the children on a high quality four year physical education journey. Embedded in this is the aim of ensuring that physical activity (PA) becomes a long term habit i.e. an infinite role in their lives to unlock and maintain its lifelong benefits. We want to create a social mission of ‘Don’t stop moving’ that brings a simple meaning to our PESA aims. PE for living life everyday. Our PESA curriculum is supportive and inclusive for all children; that values movement, positive attitudes and thinking skills. Our aim is to provide high quality educational experiences that are authentic and meaningful to their lives so they can be educated citizens allowing each child to lead an autonomous, authentic life, fully in touch with their feelings and body in a crowded world of media, cultural and social expectations.
What we do
The school timetable ensures that each academic year the Children receive two hourly lessons of PE per week. All year groups take part in swimming for a full term with lessons of 30 minutes each Friday.
Swimming
All year groups receive one full term of swimming lessons at Moberly Swimming Pool, Kilburn Lane. Lessons are 30 minutes with the children in groups of 10 or less. Swimming is a curricular activity and as such pupils cannot opt out of the lessons.
By the end of year 6, we want to ensure that every child can swim at least 25 metres.
The importance of learning swimming and water safety is a key part of growing up. It allows young people to have fun in the water with family and friends. Learning about water safety is an essential life-saving skill and is vital to staying safe in and around water. Knowing how to swim provides access to many other water-related activities and careers.
True or False: Being Exposed to Wet, Cold Weather Increases the Risk of Infection
THE IMPORTANCE OF LEARNING SWIMMING AND WATER SAFETY SKILLS AT KEY STAGE 1 OR 2 A GUIDE FOR PARENTS
Kilburn Park School Awarded School Games Silver Mark Award
Kilburn Park School is delighted to announce that it has been awarded the School Games Silver Mark Award for the 2024-25 academic year. The award recognises the school’s dedication to high-quality physical education and inclusive sporting opportunities.
The School Games Mark is a government-led awards scheme, funded by Sport England and delivered by the Youth Sport Trust, that celebrates schools’ commitment to the development of competition, leadership and physical activity. Since its launch in 2006, the initiative has supported over 13 million opportunities for young people across England.
With more than 19,000 schools registered, the School Games works with local and county-level organisers to embed physical activity into the school day. The focus is on engaging less active young people and creating inclusive, accessible opportunities for all pupils, regardless of background or ability.
Brent Schools Sport Partnership
The school are part of the Harris Lowe Academy/Kingsbury High School, Brent schools sports partnership. This membership allows for the children to take part in various sporting events throughout their time at the school. Events are held at Capital City Academy, Willesden Sports Centre and Kingsbury High School. There is over 25 events per academic year that we bring the children along to.

Admission Arrangements
No child will be refused admission to school on the basis of his or her special educational need, ethnicity or language need. In line with the Equalities Act 2010, we will not discriminate against disabled children and we will take all reasonable steps to provide effective educational provision (see Admission policy for the school, as agreed with the Local Authority)

Click on the Brent Local Offer link to find out more about support and information that is offered in the Brent Community.

Art & Design
Our teaching in Art & Design aims to provide children with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design.
Art & Design is taught as a discrete subject by a specialist teacher. There are six strands of learning in Art & Design
